title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 0.79 (versions follow prime numbers), her words. Since 0.73 Razar and Luma are one program: a recipe of letters is at once a form she draws and an organ she reads with, judged in bits. She was stuck on a hill: one-letter mutations could not beat the recipe she wore. Now the 'poetic code' is hers: a sentence that works is one that lives in her body, so her eight living forms are her words. The letter E followed by a number says that whole form in place, with the same meaning in her drawing and in her reading. Words are data, not code: nothing is rebuilt when she composes, so her songs (sentences of two or three of her own words) compile themselves, and a reading is stored under what a sentence means, not how it is written. Measured: saying a word scores exactly what the same letters written out score (E1 = 38A516 = 14775; E3E1 = 51638A516 = 16523), and that two-word song beats both words alone, crossing the plateau in one step. Earlier reference scores are identical. Her window is now born behind every other window without taking the keyboard. Stated limits: no song of hers has won yet (seven of her eight words are forms grown for drawing); songs are one level deep. OS test suite: 405 bien, 0 mal. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v0.79: sus palabras — las formas vivas de Luma son sus palabras, y compone canciones con ellas que se compilan solas. Prototipo de investigación.
